notes: Shipping lanes: Benden, P. (2022), Global Shipping Lanes, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.6361763 (CC BY 4.0), traced from the CIA's Map of the World's Oceans. Chokepoints and ports: written for this site; figures are approximate.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Dover (English Channel)
chokepoints.text: The world's busiest shipping lane: hundreds of ships pass every day between the North Sea and the Atlantic, so traffic is split into lanes, like a motorway.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Gibraltar
chokepoints.text: The only sea link between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic, 14 km wide at its narrowest. Ships to and from the Suez Canal pass through it.

chokepoints.name: Bosporus and Dardanelles (Turkish Straits)
chokepoints.text: The only route from the Black Sea to the world's oceans, running through the middle of Istanbul. Ukraine's and Russia's grain and oil exports depend on it.

chokepoints.name: Suez Canal
chokepoints.text: A canal through Egypt (opened 1869) linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, so ships between Europe and Asia avoid sailing around Africa. About 12–15% of world trade normally uses it. When the ship Ever Given blocked it in 2021, global trade was disrupted for weeks.

chokepoints.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
chokepoints.text: The narrow strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal. Attacks on ships by the Houthi movement since late 2023 have made many shipping companies send ships the long way around Africa.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.text: The only sea route out of the Persian Gulf. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar and Iran, so any threat to close it affects oil prices worldwide.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Malacca
chokepoints.text: Between Malaysia and the Indonesian island of Sumatra, the shortest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Tens of thousands of ships a year carry oil to China, Japan and South Korea and goods back to Europe. Singapore, at its southern end, grew rich on this trade.

chokepoints.name: Taiwan Strait
chokepoints.text: Between mainland China and Taiwan; a busy route for ships between north-east Asia and the rest of the world, and a centre of tension between China and Taiwan.

chokepoints.name: Panama Canal
chokepoints.text: A canal (opened 1914) across Panama linking the Atlantic and Pacific, saving ships a long voyage around South America. About 5% of world sea trade uses it. Its locks need fresh water from a lake; a drought in 2023 forced it to limit the number of ships.

chokepoints.name: Cape of Good Hope
chokepoints.text: The southern tip of Africa: the long way round between Europe and Asia, used by the biggest ships and by many more when the Red Sea route is dangerous.

chokepoints.name: Danish Straits
chokepoints.text: The narrow channels linking the Baltic Sea with the North Sea, used by ships from Russia, Finland, Sweden, Poland and the Baltic states.
